title: Music, sound effects and mix
purpose: Measures music presence, tempo, level under the voice, ducking, sound effects and loudness, and writes a mix recipe and a licence-safe music brief.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: A1 spectrograms (full band and highpassed), A3 momentary loudness, A5 side vs mid loudness for music under voice (stereo only), A6 RMS in speech gaps.
pitfalls: Naming a commercial track; never identify or reuse it
Using side-channel loudness on a mono source
Calling every onset a sound effect

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.text: one technique description, at most 300 characters, no copied content
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"
recipes.A3: Momentary loudness every 100 ms (LUFS): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/lufs_m.txt" -f null -
recipes.A5: Side (L-R) channel loudness, which removes centre-panned voice and leaves most stereo music: replace the A3 filter with "pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0-0.5*c1,ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/side_m.txt"; mid channel uses 0.5*c0+0.5*c1. Only meaningful for stereo sources.
recipes.A6: RMS level per 100 ms at 48 kHz: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "aresample=48000,asetnsamples=n=4800,astats=metadata=1:reset=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level:file=$WORK/rms.txt" -f null -

questions.question: Is there music, and what share of the runtime does it cover?
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrograms in 5 s windows across the video (sustained tonal or rhythmic content); for stereo sources A5 side loudness above -50 LUFS also indicates music.
questions.challenge: Ambience and room tone are not music; require tonal or rhythmic structure.

questions.question: What is the music tempo in BPM?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills music tempo for beat-synced edits.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.audio.tempo_bpm (video_re_onsets_beats); verify by counting onsets on an A1 spectrogram over 10 s.
questions.challenge: Tempo estimators often double or halve; check the manual count.

questions.question: What is the instrumentation class (piano, acoustic guitar, strings or orchestral, synth pads, electronic beat, lo-fi, percussion only)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the music brief for licensed or original replacement music; never identifies the track.
questions.how_to_answer: Describe from A1 spectrograms (harmonic patterns, percussion transients) and frame-independent listening cues; method inferred.
questions.challenge: Answers that name the track, artist or album are rejected.

questions.question: How many dB below the voice does the music sit during speech?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills music_under_voice_db (a common house target is about 18 dB).
questions.how_to_answer: Stereo: A5 side loudness versus mid loudness during speech segments (approximation). Otherwise compare A6 RMS in speech gaps (music only) with RMS during speech, noting the music level may change (ducking).
questions.challenge: State the method; ducking makes the gap method overestimate music under voice.

questions.question: Is the music ducked under speech, and by how many dB?
questions.how_to_answer: A5 side loudness (or music band energy on A1) just before and during speech onsets at 4 points.
questions.challenge: Musical dynamics change on their own; check that drops align with speech onsets in most cases.

questions.question: What is the integrated loudness of the whole mix?
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.audio.integrated_lufs (video_re_audio_loudness).
questions.challenge: Recompute with ffmpeg ebur128 summary if the value looks implausible.

questions.question: What is the loudness range (LRA)?
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.audio.loudness_range.
questions.challenge: Recompute with ebur128 if missing.

questions.question: What is the true peak, and is there clipping?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a peak limit in the mix recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: ffmpeg -i SRC -af ebur128=peak=true -f null - (summary true peak); A2 waveform for flat tops.
questions.challenge: Lossy encoding can push true peak above 0; report the codec.

questions.question: How does the music evolve (intro, build, drop at the hook or payoff, steady loop)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a music structure rule aligned with beats.
questions.how_to_answer: A3 momentary loudness of the side channel (or full mix in gaps) over time; mark rises and drops with timestamps.
questions.challenge: Separate voice-driven loudness from music changes.

questions.question: Does the music change between beats (new track or section per item)?
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrograms at beat boundaries: changes in key, instrumentation or tempo.
questions.challenge: Check 3 boundaries.

questions.question: Which sound effect types occur (whoosh, pop, click, ding, riser, impact, typewriter, camera shutter, swoosh-up), with counts?
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrograms with highpass=f=3000 at visual events (cuts, text pops); onsets not explained by music or speech.
questions.challenge: Each type needs at least one timestamp; music percussion is not sfx.

questions.question: How many sound effects per minute are used?
questions.how_to_answer: Count from 011 / duration x 60.
questions.challenge: Report total count and duration.

questions.question: What share of sound effects align with a visual event (within 80 ms)?
questions.how_to_answer: Match sfx timestamps with cuts, text entrances and transitions.
questions.challenge: Report the matching tolerance and chance rate.

questions.question: How does the music end (ends on a final hit with the video, fades out, cut mid-phrase)?
questions.how_to_answer: A1 and A3 over the last 3 s.
questions.challenge: Check whether the fade is in the music itself or applied in the mix (fade starts before content ends).

questions.question: What mood does the music support, described by measurable features (tempo, mode if apparent, density)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the music brief for replacement music.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine tempo (002), instrumentation (003) and loudness (009); mode (major/minor) only if clearly audible from harmonic content; method inferred.
questions.challenge: Mood words must be tied to features; 'epic' alone is taste.

questions.question: Is silence used as emphasis (music cut out right before a reveal)?
questions.how_to_answer: A3 drops of over 10 LU lasting 0.2-1 s before payoff moments.
questions.challenge: Each drop must be followed by a reveal within 1.5 s.

questions.question: How wide is the music's stereo image (side/mid loudness ratio)?
questions.how_to_answer: A5 side versus mid loudness in music-only gaps.
questions.challenge: Mono sources make this 0; check A7 channels.

questions.question: How heavy is the low end (energy below 150 Hz relative to the full band)?
questions.how_to_answer: A6 RMS with lowpass=f=150 versus unfiltered, in music-only gaps.
questions.challenge: Report both RMS values.

questions.question: Are risers used before reveals, and how long are they?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds risers to the sfx plan.
questions.how_to_answer: A1: rising pitch or noise sweeps ending at reveals.
questions.challenge: Report timestamps and lengths.

questions.question: Are ambience beds used (ocean, crowd, wind, room) under the music or voice?
questions.how_to_answer: A1: broadband noise textures consistent with the scene; F1 frames for the matching visual.
questions.challenge: Encoder noise is not ambience.

questions.question: Does the music loop, and what is the loop length?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills loop length for music editing.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare A1 spectrogram patterns in successive windows for repetition.
questions.challenge: Report the repeat points.

questions.question: Does the music mask the voice's intelligibility band (about 1-4 kHz) during speech?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an EQ rule (dip music in the voice band).
questions.how_to_answer: A1 during speech: music energy in 1-4 kHz relative to voice harmonics.
questions.challenge: Inferred from images; confidence under 0.6.

questions.question: Write the mix recipe (music level under voice, ducking, sfx level, target loudness, peak limit).
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a reproducible mix.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine 004, 005, 006 and 008, for example 'music -18 dB under voice; duck 6 dB with 150 ms attack; sfx peaks 6 dB under voice; master to {target_lufs} LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP'.
questions.challenge: Every number must come from a measurement or be marked as a default.

questions.question: Which audio parameters should a new video set (music track asset with licence, bpm range, music under voice, sfx set, target LUFS)?
questions.how_to_answer: Collect 002, 004, 006 and 011; the track is an asset slot that requires a licence field.
questions.challenge: No parameter may point to the source's music.

questions.question: How long are audio fade-ins and fade-outs at the start and end?
questions.how_to_answer: A3 at the first and last 3 s.
questions.challenge: Report ms for both.

questions.question: Do music downbeats or section changes coincide with item boundaries?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare A3 or onset clusters with beat boundaries; share within 1/8 beat.
questions.challenge: Compare with chance.

questions.question: What are the audio stream facts (codec, sample rate, channels, bitrate)?
questions.how_to_answer: A7 stream info.
questions.challenge: Copy values exactly from ffprobe.

questions.question: Do any sound effects peak louder than the voice?
questions.how_to_answer: A6 RMS at sfx moments versus median speech RMS.
questions.challenge: Report the levels.

questions.question: Is there a sonic logo or jingle at the start or end?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a sonic-logo slot a new series fills with its own sound.
questions.how_to_answer: A1 at the first and last 3 s for a short distinctive motif.
questions.challenge: Never reuse the source's motif; the slot must be new.

questions.question: Is the music a recognisable commercial track that cannot be reused?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the rights flag on the music slot.
questions.how_to_answer: Do not identify the track. Classify only by cues (vocals with lyrics, high production with distinctive hook) and mark inferred; in all cases the variant uses separately licensed or original music.
questions.challenge: Any track name or artist in the answer is rejected.
